title: Rotary Screw Compressor
model_title: Oil-Injected Rotary Screw Compressor Package (4/6 Lobe Rotors)

introduction.definition: A rotary screw compressor compresses gas between two meshing helical rotors. Gas fills the lobe spaces at the inlet, is sealed off and carried along the rotors while the pocket shrinks, then leaves through the discharge port. Oil-injected machines use oil to seal, cool and lubricate; it is separated afterwards.
applications: Plant and instrument air (most common industrial compressor)
Gas boosting (fuel gas, flare gas recovery)
key_points: Few wear parts — long service intervals
Built-in volume ratio set by the ports
Oil separator and oil quality are critical

classification.type: Twin-screw, oil-injected, single stage, direct drive

introduction.summary: An oil-injected rotary screw compressor uses two meshing helical rotors. Gas fills the spaces between the lobes at the inlet end; as the rotors turn the pocket is sealed, carried along and made smaller until it opens to the discharge port. Injected oil seals, cools and lubricates; it is then separated from the air in the separator vessel and returned.

The male rotor (driven by the motor) turns the female rotor; a pocket of air is sealed between the lobes and the casing.

steps.text: Air enters through the filter and inlet valve into the lobes at the inlet end.
The male rotor (driven by the motor) turns the female rotor; a pocket of air is sealed between the lobes and the casing.
As the rotors turn, the pocket moves toward the discharge end and its volume shrinks — pressure rises.
Oil injected into the pockets seals the clearances and absorbs the heat of compression.
The air–oil mixture leaves through the discharge port to the separator vessel; clean air goes to service and oil returns.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Flow almost constant with pressure; specific power (kW per m³/min) is the key efficiency measure (ISO 1217 Annex C/E).

pressure.title: Pressure along the rotors
pressure.description: Air trapped between the lobes is carried from the inlet end toward the discharge end; the pocket shrinks and the pressure rises until the pocket reaches the discharge port (built-in volume ratio).

components.key_components: Male & female rotors, rotor casing, bearings, inlet valve, oil separator

parts.name: Rotor Casing (Inlet Port top, Discharge Port bottom)
parts.function: Encloses the rotors with tight clearances; contains inlet and discharge ports.

parts.name: Male Rotor (4 lobes) — driven by the motor
parts.function: Driven rotor; with the female rotor it forms shrinking pockets of gas.

parts.name: Female Rotor (6 flutes)
parts.function: Meshes with the male rotor and is driven through the oil film.

parts.name: Rotor Bearings (radial rollers + discharge-end thrust bearings)
parts.function: Locate rotors radially and carry the axial gas thrust.

parts.name: Flexible Coupling
parts.function: Transmits torque between motor and pump while accommodating small misalignment and allowing separation for maintenance.
parts.material: Steel or cast iron hubs; elastomer or stainless-steel disc elements.

parts.name: Coupling Guard
parts.material: Steel, aluminium or non-sparking brass for hazardous areas.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Frame & End Shields
parts.function: Encloses the stator and supports the bearings; feet or flange mount the motor to the baseplate or pump.
parts.material: Cast iron or aluminium frame; steel fasteners.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Stator
parts.material: Silicon electrical steel, copper magnet wire, Class F/H insulation (typical).

parts.name: Electric Motor – Rotor & Shaft
parts.function: Converts the rotating field into shaft torque (squirrel-cage induction rotor).
parts.material: Electrical steel, die-cast aluminium or copper.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Bearings (DE & NDE)
parts.function: Support the motor rotor at drive and non-drive ends.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Cooling Fan
parts.function: Draws cooling air over the finned frame.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Fan Cover
parts.function: Guards the fan and directs air along the fins.

parts.name: Air Filter & Inlet (Suction-Throttle) Valve
parts.function: Cleans incoming air and controls capacity (load/unload or modulation).

parts.name: Oil Separator Vessel, Separator Element & Oil Sump
parts.function: Separates oil from the compressed air and stores the oil.

parts.name: Discharge Line, Oil Injection Line & Service Air Outlet
parts.function: Carries air/oil mixture to the separator, oil back to injection, and air to service.

parts.name: Baseplate
parts.function: Provides a rigid common mounting for pump and driver, maintains alignment and transfers loads to the foundation.
parts.material: Carbon steel, painted; stainless steel for hygienic or corrosive areas.

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Use an air receiver, dryer and filters per the required ISO 8573-1 class; slope pipework to drains.
Provide enough ventilation to remove the compressor heat (or recover it).
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

routine.task: Check oil level, discharge temperature and separator ΔP.

periodic.task: Change oil, oil filter, air filter and separator element per running hours.

overhaul.task: Replace rotor bearings and shaft seal (airend overhaul).

lubrication: Compressor oil (mineral or synthetic) as specified; oil also lubricates the bearings.

causes: Low oil, blocked oil cooler, high ambient
remedies: Top up oil, clean cooler, improve ventilation

causes: Separator element failed, high oil level, scavenge line blocked

A rotary screw compressor compresses gas between two meshing helical rotors.
Gas fills the lobe spaces at the inlet, is sealed off and carried along the rotors while the pocket shrinks, then leaves through the discharge port.
Oil-injected machines use oil to seal, cool and lubricate; it is separated afterwards.
Typical applications include plant and instrument air (most common industrial compressor); refrigeration and heat pumps; gas boosting (fuel gas, flare gas recovery); mobile construction compressors.

Air enters through the filter and inlet valve into the lobes at the inlet end.

As the rotors turn, the pocket moves toward the discharge end and its volume shrinks — pressure rises.
Oil injected into the pockets seals the clearances and absorbs the heat of compression.
The air–oil mixture leaves through the discharge port to the separator vessel; clean air goes to service and oil returns.

video_tutorials.title: Rotary Screw Compressor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Rotary Screw Compressor.
Check oil level, discharge temperature and separator ΔP.
Change oil, oil filter, air filter and separator element per running hours.
Check inlet valve function.
Replace rotor bearings and shaft seal (airend overhaul).
Watch for high discharge temperature: trips on temperature. Common cause: low oil, blocked oil cooler, high ambient.
Watch for oil carry-over: oil in the air system. Common cause: separator element failed, high oil level, scavenge line blocked.
Watch for bearing wear: rising vibration and noise. Common cause: age, oil contamination.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
